pattern.name: Entrance Transition
pattern.paraphrase: Arriving home goes through a distinct in-between space rather than straight from the street to the door.

derived.from: Tucson, Pima County, Arizona, United States
derived.note: Derived from the location the film discloses, not stated by the film.

count.text: The founders initially considered putting their two houses on a shared piece of land.

age.text: A resident reports living here for 23 years.
A resident moved from Wisconsin, having drawn communities as a child and fallen in love with the Sonoran Desert at age five.
Beth’s family moved here when her daughter was nine years old.
A resident raised her children in the Midwest and moved to Tucson at age 44, later growing to love it.

build time.text: The description says 28 households have spent 28 years building the community.
build time.doubt: The description’s 28-year account differs from the film’s 1993 starting point; the periods described may be different.

places.title: An artist couple’s narrow Tokyo home

derived.note: Derived from the location the film discloses, not stated by the film.

instances.title: Beth’s deep shaded entrance porch
instances.description: A broad roof shelters Beth’s recessed entry, bench and seating. Beth says she loved the deep porch and relates porch depth to the homes’ passive-solar design.
instances.unknown: No dimensions or measured solar exposure are provided; compass directions are reported, not independently checked.

assignment.basis: A deep roofed porch with a bench sits between the shared path and the front door.

instances.title: Street-front gallery and study gatehouse
instances.description: A tall narrow building has a gallery below and a study reached by ladder above. Masahiro calls it a gatehouse, while the description identifies it as both entryway and offices.
instances.unknown: Its foundation, insulation and overall dimensions are not shown.

claims.text: Upper gatehouse is the husband’s study.
Gatehouse combines entryway, art gallery and offices.
A small wooden ladder accesses the upper study.
claims.doubt: The description says wooden, but the reviewed frames show a gray metallic-looking round-rung ladder.

assignment.basis: A separate street-front building is passed on the way to the main house.

instances.title: Planted courtyard and narrow approach
instances.description: Gravel paths, low groundcover, shrubs and a small tree occupy the gaps around the gatehouse and main-house entrance. Continuous walking shots show the narrow approach in use.
instances.unknown: Exact boundaries, plant species and garden maintenance are not established.

assignment.basis: A planted gravel approach runs between the gatehouse and the main-house door.

instances.title: Entry steps down to lower rooms
instances.description: The camera follows the entry down toward the bathroom and bedroom. Masahiro explains that lowering the floor kept the building height within code.
instances.unknown: The amount of lowering and ground-water protection are not established.

claims.text: Lower floor was sunk to meet the building-height limit.

assignment.basis: The way in steps down to the lower rooms, a change of level after the door.

sentences.text: Tucson’s roofed porch and Tokyo’s gatehouse, planted approach and lowered entry all follow the pattern, in derived hot desert and humid subtropical climates respectively.
Beth loved the deep porch and links its depth to passive-solar design; Masahiro says lowering Tokyo’s floor met the building-height limit.
The porch shelters a bench between path and door; the gatehouse combines entry, gallery and offices.
Tokyo’s planted gravel approach is shown but not discussed.
Neither film establishes costs or failures for these entrance features.
Porch dimensions and measured solar exposure, garden maintenance and protection against groundwater at the lowered entry remain unknown.
